extracted.intended_audience: electric cooperative leaders, policymakers, regulatory staff, and other energy-sector stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Industry news and advocacy describing policy positions, regulatory comment themes, and best practices for electric cooperatives when engaging with federal agencies (DOE, FERC, EPA), Congress, and the public on reliability, affordability, permitting, and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect hydropower assets to preserve affordable, reliable power
rubrics_metrics.description: Hydropower assets (e.g., the Lower Snake River dams) provide low-cost, reliable, carbon-free electricity and also offer navigation, irrigation and recreation benefits; policy actions that reduce output or breach dams would harm farmers, transportation and rural communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate against policies that decrease electric output or pave the way for dam breaching; emphasize Congress’s ultimate authority; highlight regional economic and reliability impacts when making the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support bulk power system reliability in regulatory policies
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC and other agency policies regarding interconnection and large loads must support bulk power system reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing comments, emphasize how proposed rules or standardized policies affect overall system reliability; ask that interconnection/adoption policies prioritize reliability outcomes and avoid measures that could weaken bulk-system resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect importance of local control over retail electric sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal actions should not intrude on state and local authority over retail electric sales to large loads and co-op customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request that agencies preserve state/local prerogatives or provide regional flexibility rather than imposing uniform federal retail-sales rules; in comments, argue for deference to local governance and solutions tailored to co-op structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large loads should 'pay their own way' for interconnection and upgrades
rubrics_metrics.description: Large loads connecting to the interstate transmission system should bear the costs of interconnection and necessary upgrades rather than saddling other transmission customers (including co-op consumer-members) with stranded costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comments to demand cost-allocation rules that charge large loads for direct interconnection costs, and to request protections preventing other customers from shouldering upgrades for loads that fail to materialize or underutilize capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow regional flexibility in how large customers are served
rubrics_metrics.description: If FERC or other agencies seek new authority over serving large loads, they should permit regional flexibility in how those customers are served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for rules that enable regionally tailored solutions and avoid one-size-fits-all mandates; request grandfathering or flexibility mechanisms where local systems or contracts differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-of-government alignment to enable co-ops to serve large loads while protecting affordability and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal regulations, policies and incentives should be aligned across agencies to allow cooperatives and utilities to make investments needed to serve large loads at scale while protecting affordability and reliability for all customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interagency comment letters, urge coordinated policy making and incentives (tax credits, funding, permitting reforms) that reduce investment risk for co-ops tasked with serving data centers and other big loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting reform to shorten timelines and reduce litigation delays (SPEED Act principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting reform should shorten permitting timelines, reduce frivolous litigation that holds up infrastructure projects, and modernize NEPA implementation so it is less complex, unpredictable and unworkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support legislation and agency rulemaking that streamlines review processes, clarifies triggers for NEPA, and focuses reviews on direct, foreseeable impacts; in advocacy, quantify economic and reliability harms from current delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not automatically trigger NEPA review based solely on federal grants/funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving federal grants or other types of funding should not automatically trigger a NEPA review for co-op improvement projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose statutory or regulatory language excluding routine grant-funded upgrades from full NEPA review, or creating categorical exclusions for common co-op projects to reduce unnecessary delay and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit NEPA to direct, foreseeable environmental impacts within agency expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA reviews should concentrate on direct, foreseeable environmental impacts that fall within an agency's expertise and legal mandate rather than expansive or speculative analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on NEPA procedures, request narrower scope standards, clearer thresholds for significance, and agency guidance to avoid overbroad environmental review that delays projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend compliance timelines and seek implementation input for costly/unproven rules (EPA wastewater/regional haze guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules that impose high costs or require unproven technologies (e.g., EPA's power plant wastewater rule), agencies should extend compliance timelines and seek public input on how to streamline implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File comments asking for extended deadlines, phased approaches, flexibility mechanisms, and opportunities to comment on implementation details to avoid premature retirements of needed generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory standards must be achievable and lawful (opposition to unachievable GHG limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions standards (e.g., 90% carbon capture requirements, forced co-firing percentages) must be achievable in real-world operation and legally sound; unachievable rules risk forcing early retirement of essential generation and impairing reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge rules in comments that set unattainable performance metrics; provide technical and economic evidence of infeasibility and request alternative, practicable standards or repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support funding and programs to preserve and modernize always-available generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal financial support (grants, loans, targeted funding) should be available to recommission or modernize coal and other always-available plants, support wastewater management systems, and enable co-firing or other transitional measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for direct funding programs (e.g., DOE allocations) in comments and legislative letters, and document how targeted funding preserves reliability and affordability while managing environmental impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require freeze protection and cold-weather preparedness for fuel and generation reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas utilities and generators should prepare for severe cold with freeze protection measures and other cold-weather preparedness plans to avoid fuel and generation shortfalls during extreme winter conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage agencies and industry standards bodies to adopt mandatory winterization requirements, and include preparedness planning in comments as a necessary reliability measure (cite NERC recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design transmission projects for resilience against extreme weather
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission projects should use materials and designs (e.g., conductors more resistant to icing, stronger structures and foundations) to withstand extraordinary wind speeds and icing to enhance resiliency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When supporting or permitting projects, emphasize climate/resiliency design standards and reference engineering choices that reduce outage risk under extreme weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early and meaningful community engagement for transmission projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful transmission projects require 'early-and-often' engagement with impacted communities, going beyond regulatory hearings—holding open houses, meeting with county boards, townships, recreational groups and one-on-one landowner meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote transparent, proactive outreach plans in project permitting and in comments; document outreach efforts and use them to build public trust and reduce litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: UAS/drone inspection programs to improve safety, efficiency and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt drone-based inspections (digitized reports, BVLOS exemptions, partnerships with training institutions) to accelerate damage assessment, reduce field work, save costs, and support workforce development; plan for AI-assisted image analysis to speed assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design UAS programs with goals (e.g., poles inspected per flight, percent field-work reduction, annual savings), pursue BVLOS exemptions where appropriate, partner with colleges or contractors, digitize inspection reports, and pilot AI workflows for near-real-time assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend strict liability caps and expedite permitting for wildfire mitigation projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should extend utility strict liability caps for wildfire incidents on federal lands and codify expedited permitting processes for wildfire prevention projects (hazard tree removals, undergrounding) to enable timely mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate in letters and testimony for statutory extensions and codification of expedited procedures (citing Fix Our Forests Act and related bills), and explain how such reforms reduce wildfire risk and protect co-op reliability.
